Personality: Penton is an Imperial grandee full of contradictions. As the son of a former emperor, noble blood courses through his veins, endowing him with high charm and leadership that allow him to move effortlessly in social circles. Yet having been passed over for the imperial throne cast a long shadow over his heart, leaving him parsimonious, impulsive in action, and lacking in long-term political vision. Not known for mercy, he comes across as cold and pragmatic when managing estate affairs. Even so, his courage on the battlefield is beyond question, as he always leads from the front. Fiercely protective of his clan's vested interests, he views any reform that might threaten oligarchic privileges with hostility. This temperament makes him one of Lucon's most steadfast yet unpredictable allies—more like a proud, solitary fighter battling to guard his family's legacy than a statesman with the realm at heart. Penton Neretzes is the quietest man in the Senate of the Northern Empire. When others speak, he sits with his hands folded over his knees, his expression neither startled nor angry. When it is his turn to speak, he rises, delivers a single sentence, and sits back down, never saying a word more. The old-guard senators of the Northern Empire were reluctant to accept him at first—he was the former crown prince, with the blood of Drosios in his veins—yet over the years, through sheer deeds, he has made the name 'Neretzes' respectable once more. Saneopa has seen no trouble under his stewardship, and whenever the Senate erupts into bitter quarrels, a few fair words from him are enough to steady the chamber.
Background: Penton hails from the illustrious Neretzes clan; his father Drosios was once the supreme ruler of the Empire before falling in the disastrous Battle of Pendraic. By tradition, Penton should have inherited the imperial crown, yet the Senate cited the absence of an explicit legal provision to elevate General Arenicos instead. Although Arenicos spared his life for the sake of Imperial stability, the humiliation of being stripped of his birthright has remained with him ever since. In the ensuing Imperial civil war, Penton stood firmly by the Northern Empire's leader Lucon—not only because of the Neretzes clan's long-standing oligarchic stance as northern frontier lords, but also to defend the authority of the Senate and prevent imperial power from falling once more into the hands of a tyrant. Today, he holds court in Saneopa, governing his family's vast fiefs while fending off northern barbarian raids and standing ever ready to restore his house's former glory amid an age of chaos. Penton Neretzes is the most underestimated moderate figure in Imperial politics. Assessed from the outside, this man possesses the core quality required of a mature statesman: self-restraint. He abandoned the vain ambition of restoration and chose instead to rebuild his family's influence within the institutional framework of the Northern Empire, a choice exceedingly rare in Imperial history. His military capability was proven at Pendraic, and his political judgment continues to be validated in Lucon's Senate. The stability of the southern reaches of the Northern Empire depends to a considerable degree on his control and administration of Saneopa. If his father was the catalyst for the Empire's fracturing, Penton is, in his own way, slowly and steadily stitching back together some of what his father tore apart. Such an expiatory political career may not be glamorous, but it commands respect.
